Optional intruder photos can use the front camera after repeated incorrect attempts. Enable the feature and grant camera permission in Settings. Android may show a camera privacy indicator.
Learn how SafeLock detects foreground apps and requests authentication. It is not a replacement for the Android screen lock.

SafeLock adds authentication to selected apps. Lock decisions and credentials are local; the app also contacts GitHub to check for updates. Android and manufacturer restrictions can delay or stop detection.

With Usage Access granted and App Shield enabled, SafeLock polls foreground app events and requests a lock activity for protected apps. Detection is not instantaneous, and Android can restrict background activity launches.

Temporary unlocks are kept in memory. Screen-off clears them; timeout and exit settings can relock apps sooner. Use Lock apps again in the app-list options to clear temporary unlocks without changing saved locks.

Choose numeric PINs, patterns, or text passwords. Credentials are stored as salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes, not plaintext. Three incorrect credential attempts pause verification for 30 seconds across lock and settings checks.
Tap the biometric button to open Android authentication. The physical sensor location and available biometric methods depend on your device.

When enabled with camera permission, lock-screen failures can request a front-camera photo after three incorrect attempts. Capture is best-effort and may show an Android privacy indicator. Photos are private app files, not encrypted gallery records. View and delete them in Settings > View Intruder Gallery.
Protecting Settings adds a check during normal use. It cannot guarantee protection from force-stop, safe mode, permission revocation, or uninstall through Android system controls.
